content.title: About
content.content: Stewed potatoes with tomatoes is a dish made from selected potatoes, ripe tomatoes, onion and aromatic spices. The potatoes are simmered until tender, then tomatoes are added to create a rich sauce. The dish is popular in Eastern European and Mediterranean cuisines, often served as a side or a light main course.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Stewed potatoes retain most of their vitamin C when cooked gently without prolonged boiling.
Tomatoes added to the dish are rich in lycopene – an antioxidant that becomes more bioavailable after heating.
Traditionally the recipe is prepared in earthenware pots, which help preserve flavor and moisture.
In some regions sweet bell pepper or carrots are added for extra color and taste.
The dish is commonly garnished with fresh parsley or dill for a bright finish.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide slowly digestible carbs that supply steady energy and help maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C and potassium
items.content: Together potatoes and tomatoes deliver vitamin C and potassium, supporting immune function and normal blood pressure.

items.title: Lycopene and antioxidants
items.content: Cooked tomatoes increase lycopene availability, which protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The dish is typically prepared with minimal oil, making it suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Potato skins and tomatoes provide fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes, ranging from skin rashes to gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Adding excessive salt can make the dish unsuitable for people with hypertension.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Tomatoes contain oxalates, which in large amounts may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve stewed potatoes with tomatoes hot as a standalone dish or as a side to meat, fish, or legumes. Garnish with fresh herbs, drizzle a little olive oil, or sprinkle with grated cheese for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the dish to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When reheating, add a splash of water or broth to restore moisture.
